references.text: God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teem, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. The phrase 'according to its kind' (למינה) is used here in the same way as in Gen 7:14.
The creation of land animals—cattle, creeping things, and wild beasts—according to their kinds reflects the same categorization used in Gen 7:14 when the animals entered the ark.
God's command to Noah to bring animals of every kind into the ark—birds, cattle, and creeping things according to their kinds—directly prepares for the event described in Gen 7:14.
God's specific instruction to take both clean and unclean animals as well as birds into the ark is the direct reason why the animals in 7:14 actually entered the ark.
All animals, creeping things, and birds left the ark 'according to their kinds'—this directly mirrors 7:14 and shows that biodiversity was preserved through the flood.
The psalmist praises God's diverse creation, reflecting the rich variety of life that was preserved through the ark according to Gen 7:14.
A direct narrative connection showing God's covenant with all creation from entry to exit of the ark.
A thematic parallel where the animals saved from the flood are called to praise the Creator in song.
A powerful contrast showing that the same categories of animals that were saved were those that perished outside the ark.
A clear allusion where the list of creatures from the ark is used as a metaphor for God's plan to include all nations.
A theological link between creation (1:24) and preservation/restoration (7:14) of the same created order.
A direct narrative connection where God's command to go out (8:17) completes the gathering (7:14).
A theological link between creation (1:25) and preservation (7:14) of the original created order.
A direct narrative connection detailing which kinds were gathered before entering the ark.
